# FIPS crypto module inventory and compliance gap analysis for serving-stack images

## Description

Produce a complete, auditable inventory of cryptographic modules linked into
the model serving stack's images (KServe components and the Platform Operator
image), classifying each as validated or non-validated for FIPS 140-3, and
identifying which non-validated modules sit in the request path. This inventory
is the foundation artifact for image remediation, CI enforcement, and the
compliance evidence package.

## Scope

- Enumerate the serving-stack image set covered by the strategy (KServe
  component images and the Platform Operator image).
- For each image, inventory linked cryptographic libraries and modules
  (direct and transitive), with versions and provenance.
- Classify each module against FIPS 140-3 validated-module lists (validated,
  non-validated, or unknown/needs lab confirmation).
- Identify which non-validated crypto usage is in the request path
  (inference request handling) versus peripheral paths.
- Produce a gap analysis: per image, what must change to run correctly on
  FIPS-enabled clusters with validated crypto only in the request path.
- Flag any non-validated crypto found in serving runtime images outside the
  strategy's declared affected components — reported as an out-of-scope
  finding for a scope decision, not remediated here.
- Deliver the inventory in a format suitable for direct inclusion in the
  compliance evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every image in the declared serving-stack set has a complete crypto module
  inventory with versions and provenance.
- Every module is classified validated / non-validated / unknown, with the
  classification source recorded.
- Request-path non-validated crypto usage is identified per image.
- The gap analysis identifies, per image, the concrete remediation scope.
- Non-validated crypto found outside the declared affected components is
  reported as an explicit out-of-scope finding.
- The inventory artifact is reviewable and structured for reuse as evidence.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): establishes what must change for serving-stack images to run on
  FIPS-enabled clusters with validated crypto — identifies the gaps.
- HLR-2 (P0): the module inventory is an explicit component of the compliance
  evidence package.

# Remediate KServe images for FIPS 140-3 validated cryptography

## Description

Remediate the KServe component images so they run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated
crypto in the request path. This delivers the KServe half of the FIPS runtime
requirement.

## Scope

- For each KServe image identified with non-validated crypto in the module
  inventory: replace, rebase, or re-link the offending cryptographic
  dependencies onto validated modules (or remove them from the request path).
- Rebuild the affected KServe images in the midstream build pipeline.
- Verify each remediated image runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  cluster, including inference request handling (the request path).
- Preserve existing serving functionality (serverless and raw deployment
  modes per architecture context) — FIPS remediation must not regress serving
  behavior.
- Update image build attestations and test results for reuse in the compliance
  evidence package.
- Coordinate with the image rebuilds so downstream consumers of the images can
  pick up remediated versions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All remediated KServe images contain no non-validated cryptographic modules
  in the request path, per the module inventory classification.
- Remediated images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Inference request handling works end to end on a FIPS-enabled cluster in
  both serverless and raw deployment modes (InferenceService CRs reach Ready
  with correct predictor status).
- Existing serving functionality is not regressed.
- Build attestations and test results are recorded in a form suitable for the
  compliance evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): KServe images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using
  validated crypto modules, no non-validated crypto in the request path.
- HLR-2 (P0, partial): produces the build attestations and test results that
  feed the compliance evidence package.

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions on serving-stack builds

## Description

Add a gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces
non-validated cryptographic usage, so FIPS compliance cannot silently regress
once remediation lands.

## Scope

- Implement a build-time check (or extend existing build checks) that inspects
  serving-stack build artifacts/images for non-validated cryptographic module
  usage, based on the validated/non-validated classification from the module
  inventory.
- Wire the check into the serving-stack build pipelines as a gating (blocking)
  step, so a failing check fails the build.
- Make the classification data maintainable: when the validated-module list
  changes, the check's rules can be updated without re-engineering the check.
- Handle the request-path distinction from the module inventory so the gate
  enforces the same requirement the remediation delivers (no non-validated
  crypto in the request path).
- Document for build maintainers how to interpret and act on a gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated cryptographic usage
  in the request path fails the gating check.
- A compliant build passes the gating check (no false failures on remediated
  images).
- The check is gating — it blocks merge/release of failing builds, not merely
  advisory.
- The validated/non-validated classification the check uses is derived from
  and kept consistent with the module inventory.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): CI enforces FIPS regressions; a gating check fails any
  serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

Assemble the complete compliance evidence package — module inventory, build
attestations, and test results — for the model serving stack, ready for
submission through the security review board to the external certification
laboratory.

- Consolidate the module inventory (validated/non-validated classification,

- Consolidate build attestations for the remediated KServe and Platform
  Operator images.

  OpenShift clusters (including request-path verification).

  laboratory's evidence requirements (format, completeness, traceability).

  consistent, and traceable to the requirements before submission.
- Track evidence gaps (anything the lab may additionally require) as explicit
  follow-ups rather than blocking assembly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, build attestations, and
  test results for every image in the declared serving-stack scope.
- Evidence is traceable: each item links to its source artifact and the
  requirement it demonstrates.
- The package meets the submission requirements of the security review board
  process.
- Any known evidence gaps are explicitly listed with owners.

## HLR Traceability

  attestations, test results) is assembled for submission.

# Security review board submission and external lab certification

## Description

Drive the assembled compliance evidence package through the mandatory human
and third-party gates: security review board sign-off at the defined
milestones, and submission to the external accredited certification
laboratory for FIPS 140-3 validation of the model serving stack. This epic
covers the process management and engineering support for the externally
controlled certification — the review board and the laboratory, not
engineering, control the timeline.

## Scope

- Submit the compliance evidence package through the security review board at
  the defined milestones and track sign-off.
- Submit the package to the external accredited certification laboratory and
  manage the engagement (scheduling, lab questions, clarifications,
  additional evidence requests).
- Provide engineering support to the lab and review board: answer technical
  questions, reproduce results, supply additional artifacts on request.
- Track milestone status and communicate externally controlled timing
  (historical lab turnaround: six to nine months) into planning.
- Manage rework loops: if the review board or lab rejects or qualifies part
  of the evidence, route the required changes back to the owning work and
  resubmit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package passes security review board sign-off at all defined
  milestones.
- The evidence package is accepted by the external accredited certification
  laboratory for FIPS 140-3 validation.
- All review board and lab feedback items are resolved or explicitly tracked
  with owners and due dates.
- Externally controlled schedule (review-board cadence, lab turnaround) is
  visible in status reporting and reflected in delivery expectations.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): the evidence package is submitted through the security review
  board to the external certification lab.

model serving stack (KServe + Platform Operator) run on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated cryptographic modules, assembles a compliance evidence
package, submits it through the security review board to an external accredited
certification laboratory, adds CI regression enforcement, and documents the
FIPS support posture.

Triage (Step 0): neither check fired. The strategy spans two components
(KServe, Platform Operator), multiple work streams (image remediation, CI
enforcement, evidence/certification process, documentation), and HLRs at three
priority levels. Proceeded to full decomposition.
